editorial.marketOverview: As of Sunday 01:05 EST, US equity cash markets remain closed after Friday's heavy liquidation. Reuters reported Nasdaq Composite -5.28% and SOX roughly -11%; secondary closing coverage reported QQQ -5.67% and NVDA -14.01%. SOX's outsized losses versus QQQ indicate failed semiconductor leadership. Friday volatility was elevated, although published VIX closing figures differ and are not synchronized to all other indicators. No Sunday market reaction can be inferred.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the Sunday 00:14 EST snapshot, fresh review of the November 20–22 coverage and the unchanged curated Open Watch file (updated 2026-11-21T00:44:37+00:00, 174 events) found no verified new catalyst sufficient to alter the three-day path. Monday flash PMIs, Tuesday confidence and semiconductor/hardware earnings, and Wednesday's concentrated data calendar remain forward-looking risks, not observed market responses.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The bearish skew reflects a sharp Friday semiconductor underperformance, widespread selling and elevated volatility. An oversold rally could be forceful, but without Monday synchronized breadth, chip relative strength and volatility confirmation it remains a conditional scenario. NVDA investigations and export-control headlines carry risk but do not establish misconduct. A previously reported +29 bp Treasury curve proxy is stale, and neither fresh Fed probabilities nor matched oil contracts are independently verified.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: watch the cash-market reopen, SOX/SMH relative to QQQ, advance-decline breadth and VXN/VIX around 09:45 ET flash PMIs. Tuesday November 24: evaluate whether any bounce survives consumer confidence at 10:00 ET and ADI/Dell earnings. Wednesday November 25: PCE, GDP, durable goods and claims at 08:30 ET plus the 14:00 ET Beige Book create substantial two-way event risk. Base case remains bearish unless chip leadership and breadth repair together.
editorial.bullCase: A short-covering rebound may follow extreme Friday losses, especially if chipmakers stabilize, yields ease and volatility contracts. Bullish confirmation requires synchronized gains in QQQ and SOX/SMH, improving advance-decline breadth and sustained easing of VXN/VIX; a one-session bounce is insufficient.
editorial.bearCase: If semiconductor shares continue to lag QQQ, breadth remains negative and volatility fails to retreat, liquidation may continue through the early week. A hawkish Fed repricing or upside inflation surprise on Wednesday would increase Nasdaq duration sensitivity, but neither outcome has yet occurred.
